newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says U.S. impeding medicine under oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says U.S. impeding medicine under oil deal.

text.p: Iraqi Foreign Minister Mohammad Saeed al-Sahaf has accused the United States of impeding medical supplies under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, the Iraqi News Agency (INA) said on Wednesday.
"The American envoy (at the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq) has put on hold more than 40 medical contracts," al-Sahaf said in one of three letters to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
Sahaf said among these contracts was one to supply Iraq with anti-malaria pesticide agreed with a British firm.
He said Iraq was "in desperate need of such material as malaria is spreading quickly in Iraq particulary in its northern provinces".

The oil pact, which went into effect in December, allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine for Iraqis, hit by U.N. sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Food bought under the deal have been piling up in Iraq since April but only a truckload of 61,000 tonnes of medicine has reached the country so far.
Sahaf said more than 100,000 cases of malaria were registered since 1995 in northern Iraq, out of the control of his goverment since the 1991 Gulf War.
